editorial_note: Evidence dossier, not a criminal-accusation directory. Primary-source exhibit indexes can corroborate dates and identities of documents without verifying their contents. Indexed-only originals remain uninspected. This is a curated sample, not the complete Kentucky archive. v0.8 adds testimony-specific cross-references: testimony about a memo is not inspection of the memo itself. v0.9 separately indexes a 1999 sales bulletin as deposition Exhibit 40; exhibit identity is not review of its pages. v1.0 adds testimony quotations and GAO-reported bonus estimates but does not claim review of the standalone 1999 bulletin.

records.title: Confidential memo on expansion into noncancer pain
records.summary: STAT describes a memo by Purdue sales executive Michael Friedman to three Sackler family members, including Richard, on a planned strategy for reaching noncancer chronic-pain prescribers.
records.source_locator: STAT document timeline, Dec. 29, 1994 entry (reporter summary; original memo not directly inspected here).
records.caution: Reporting about a memo does not by itself establish whether the planned strategy was executed, or individual legal culpability.

corroborating_records.locator: 2015 sworn deposition exhibit index, PDF p. 1: Exhibit 13 identifies a Dec. 29, 1994 memo by Michael Friedman addressed to Mortimer, Raymond and Richard Sackler.

Richard Sackler deposition, Aug. 28, 2015, transcript pp. 103–104 (PDF page 26): questioning about Exhibit 13, its author, recipient list and expectations about FDA launch restrictions. The testimony is not inspection of the memo.

records.verification_gap: Direct page-by-page inspection of the December 29, 1994 memo remains outstanding; the original DocumentCloud link returned 403 in the research environment.

records.title: OxyContin marketing-team meeting minutes
records.summary: STAT reports that a marketing meeting emphasized reaching a broad pain-patient population and twice-daily dosing rather than limiting the product to cancer pain.
records.source_locator: STAT document timeline, March 31, 1995 entry (summary of meeting minutes).
records.caution: This is an attributed account of a meeting. The full minutes and their context still require independent review.

corroborating_records.locator: 2015 sworn deposition exhibit index, PDF p. 1: Exhibit 24 identifies Apr. 4, 1995 minutes for the Mar. 31, 1995 OxyContin Launch Team meeting.

Richard Sackler deposition, Aug. 28, 2015, transcript pp. 174–176 (PDF page 44): questions about Exhibit 24 and testimony that launch marketing was not intended to be limited to cancer pain. Not inspection of minutes.

records.verification_gap: Direct page-by-page inspection of the April 4, 1995 launch-team minutes remains outstanding; the linked DocumentCloud record returned 403 in the research environment.

records.title: Abbott and Purdue co-promotion arrangement
records.summary: GAO reported that a 1996 co-promotion agreement supplied at least 300 Abbott sales representatives in addition to Purdue’s sales force.
records.source_locator: GAO-04-110, marketing and promotion section, paragraph describing the 1996 co-promotion agreement and sales-force counts.
records.caution: Commercial co-promotion is documented. It does not itself establish misconduct by Abbott or any individual.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted source passage check; not peer review

records.title: Sales-force memo on OxyContin priorities
records.summary: STAT reports that an internal memo described how sales incentives prioritized OxyContin versus another Purdue product.
records.source_locator: STAT document timeline, Jan. 25, 1999 entry (summary of sales directive).
records.caution: Incentive descriptions should be distinguished from proof of a specific downstream health outcome.

corroborating_records.locator: Richard Sackler Aug. 28, 2015 deposition exhibit index, PDF page 2, transcript page 6, Exhibit 40, identifies a Jan. 25, 1999 bonus bulletin from Russ Gasdia relating to OxyContin and MS Contin; the bulletin itself was not inspected.
Richard Sackler 2015 deposition pp. 331–336; counsel reads excerpt of a Jan. 25, 1999 bulletin, but the original standalone bulletin has not been inspected.

records.verification_gap: Full January 25, 1999 bulletin and its distribution/payout records need direct inspection. The deposition excerpts corroborate only the statements discussed in sworn testimony.

records.title: Kentucky OxyContin Task Force recommendations
records.summary: STAT’s index describes a Kentucky task-force report addressing diversion and describing escalating concern among state officials during 2000 and 2001.
records.source_locator: STAT document timeline, Aug. 3, 2001 entry (task-force recommendations).
records.caution: A report of emerging concern does not quantify the causal contribution of a single manufacturer to all Kentucky outcomes.

records.title: GAO national audit of OxyContin marketing and diversion
records.summary: GAO examined Purdue’s marketing, federal responses, and potential contributors to abuse and diversion. GAO explicitly warned that available data were insufficient for certain geographic causal analyses.
records.source_locator: GAO-04-110, What GAO Found; Results in Brief; report published Dec. 19, 2003.
records.caution: The GAO report includes attribution and methodological limits; findings must not be converted into unsupported precise causal estimates.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted source passage check; not peer review

records.title: Kentucky files Commonwealth v. Purdue
records.summary: The UCSF–Johns Hopkins collection overview identifies the Kentucky case as No. 07-CI-01303 and says the state filed suit in October 2007 alleging improper OxyContin marketing.
records.source_locator: UCSF–JHU Kentucky Opioid Litigation Documents collection overview, Overview and Background (exact filing day not asserted).
records.caution: A complaint contains allegations, not adjudicated findings. The case settled later; settlement alone does not prove every pleaded allegation.

records.title: Kentucky physician’s sworn affidavit in civil litigation
records.summary: STAT reports that Kentucky physician William T. Fannin submitted an affidavit describing representations he says he received about OxyContin and his belief about adverse effects.
records.source_locator: STAT document timeline, July 2014 entry (affidavit discussed in coverage).
records.caution: Sworn testimony is evidence of what the affiant asserted; it is not a judicial finding that every stated causal claim is correct.

records.title: Kentucky litigation settlement
records.summary: The UCSF–Johns Hopkins archive overview reports that Commonwealth of Kentucky v. Purdue settled in late 2015 for $24 million.
records.source_locator: UCSF–JHU Kentucky Opioid Litigation Documents collection overview, case background.
records.caution: The archive reports settlement in late 2015, not a specific date; January 1 is only a year-sorting key, not an asserted event date. Settlement alone does not prove each allegation.

records.title: Richard Sackler email on OxyContin growth and pain specialists
records.record_type: Internal email preserved as deposition exhibit
records.summary: An archived May 30, 1999 email from Richard Sackler to Cornelia Hentzsch about proposed office space includes his expressed commitment to OxyContin’s commercial success and discussion of relationships with pain specialists and a possible gala invitation. It is an author statement in an email, not proof of any inducement or misconduct by the clinicians mentioned.
records.source_locator: UCSF archive document frcf0232, downloadable PDF page 1 (displayed exhibit page 89; Bates PDD9570163). Email within chain dated May 30, 1999, under subject “RE: New office”; paragraph starting “You won’t believe how committed...” and subsequent gala discussion.
records.caution: The correspondence contains Richard Sackler’s own characterization of business relationships. It neither verifies a financial arrangement with named clinicians nor establishes any crime, causal health outcome, or personal motivation beyond the statement itself.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted original PDF page/image inspection; not peer review

records.title: Richard Sackler deposition: exhibit index identifies early OxyContin documents
records.summary: The original Pike County deposition transcript dated August 28, 2015 identifies two earlier Purdue records in its exhibit list: Exhibit 13, a December 29, 1994 memorandum from Michael Friedman to Mortimer, Raymond and Richard Sackler; and Exhibit 24, an April 4, 1995 memo recording the March 31 launch-team meeting. This establishes how the documents were identified as exhibits, not the truth of every statement in them.
records.source_locator: UCSF archive item hjdf0232, PDF page 1 (four transcript pages printed on scan): deposition title/dated cover, transcript exhibit index at printed pages 3 and 4. Exhibit 13 listed on printed p. 3; Exhibit 24 listed on printed p. 4. Only the exhibit index was visually inspected for this record.
records.caution: Exhibit identification is independently visible in the transcript index. The complete 1994 memorandum and 1995 meeting minutes have not been independently inspected here, and the exhibit list by itself does not prove their descriptions, implementation, illegality, or causal effects.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted inspection of PDF page 1 exhibit index; not peer review

records.title: Richard Sackler testimony about the 1994 marketing-strategy memo
records.summary: In Kentucky litigation testimony, Richard Sackler identified Michael Friedman as head of sales and marketing in 1994 and agreed that the December 1994 memo was directed to Mortimer, Raymond and himself. When questioned about an anticipated FDA restriction to cancer pain, he said that was Friedman’s expectation, not his own. These are statements in a deposition, not independent inspection of the original memorandum.
records.source_locator: UCSF archive ID hjdf0232, Richard Sackler deposition (Aug. 28, 2015), transcript pp. 103–104, PDF page 26, examination of Plaintiff’s Exhibit 13. Source text contains questions as well as answers; distinguish each. Text passage checked; scanned page 26 not independently image-reviewed.
records.caution: The witness’s answers support the described identity and historical statements. They do not prove that he approved the memo, that the plan was executed as written, or that the original memo’s full contents have been independently checked. Counsel’s questions are not automatically accepted facts.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted deposition text locator check; not peer review
records.verification_gap: Inspect Exhibit 13 itself, including every page and any attachments, before calling its contents primary-inspected.

records.title: Richard Sackler testimony about the 1995 launch-team minutes
records.summary: In his 2015 deposition, Richard Sackler was questioned about April 4, 1995 minutes of a March 31 launch-team meeting. Asked whether the marketing strategy was to avoid limiting OxyContin to cancer pain, he answered affirmatively, and discussed market pressures from generic competition to MS Contin. These are attributed testimony and excerpted readings, not direct examination of the complete minutes.
records.source_locator: UCSF archive ID hjdf0232, Richard Sackler deposition (Aug. 28, 2015), transcript pp. 174–176, PDF page 44, questioning on Plaintiff’s Exhibit 24. The question on p. 174 paraphrases launch strategy; the witness answers on p. 176. Source text checked, but the PDF page image and original minutes were not independently inspected.
records.caution: Deposition testimony is evidence of what the witness said; a lawyer’s reading of a document does not replace inspection of the entire original. It does not on its own establish specific patient harm or criminal liability.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted deposition text locator check; not peer review
records.verification_gap: Review the original Exhibit 24 minutes, especially surrounding context, intended audiences, and dates, before any direct-memo-content certification.

records.title: Deposition discussion of first-quarter 1999 OxyContin and MS Contin incentive weights
records.record_type: Sworn deposition transcript – sales bulletin discussion
records.summary: In an August 28, 2015 Kentucky deposition, counsel read portions of an identified January 25, 1999 Russ Gasdia sales bulletin into the record. Counsel described first-quarter 1999 MS Contin sales/quota weighting of $0.50 per sales dollar and OxyContin weighting of $1.15 per sales dollar. Richard Sackler interpreted it as a shift in sales incentives while also expressing uncertainty about details and recollection.
records.source_locator: UCSF archive hjdf0232, deposition transcript PDF page labeled 84, printed transcript pages 331–336, especially pp. 333–335: counsel reads Jan. 25, 1999 bulletin weighting ($0.50/$1 MS Contin; $1.15/$1 OxyContin); witness responds on pp. 333–335. Extracted transcript text checked; scanned page image not independently inspected.
records.caution: This directly documents questions, quoted bulletin excerpts and a witness response in a sworn deposition; it does not independently authenticate the entire 1999 bulletin, establish amounts actually paid, establish the impact on any patient, or prove criminal liability.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted extracted transcript text review; not peer review

records.title: GAO report on OxyContin-linked sales incentive estimates, 1996 and 2001
records.record_type: Government oversight report – sales incentives section
records.summary: GAO-04-110 reported that Purdue-estimated total sales bonuses tied to OxyContin rose from about $1 million in 1996 to about $40 million in 2001. GAO separately described quotas, sales-force growth and average 2001 salary and bonus levels; the two OxyContin-linked totals are reported estimates, not an audit of payments made to any particular representative.
records.source_locator: GAO-04-110 (Dec. 19, 2003), section “Purdue Significantly Increased Its Sales Force to Market and Promote OxyContin”, paragraphs beginning “Purdue stated it offered a better than industry average salary” and “The amount of total bonuses that Purdue estimated were tied to OxyContin sales” (accessible HTML around lines 970–989).
records.caution: The $1m and $40m figures are Purdue estimates reported by GAO for two different years. They are not inflation-adjusted, not a continuous annual series, and neither the bonus totals nor their change directly establishes a specific health outcome or individual wrongdoing.
records.reviewer: OAA369 AI-assisted source text passage check; not peer review
